newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates close steady.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates close steady.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed steady on Monday as exporters and spinners went to the sidelines to digest Friday's 1997/98 (July-June) budget, dealers at the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said.

Dealer Nasim Usman said exporters were unhappy because the government had ignored their demand for abolition of 10 percent sales tax, applicable on local sales and refundable on export. Exporters say getting refunds takes time and blocks funds.
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 variety was quoted at 2,125/2,250 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), K-68 at 2,425/2,450 and MNH-93 at 2,425/2,450.

The KCA said exporters had shipped 74,224 375-lb bales of cotton by May 28 compared to 1.81 million at the same time a year ago. Exporters had registered contracts for the export of 110,304 bales by June 11 compared to 2.32 million last year.
